title: Assist route-glow halo still sizes from the pre-band wire formula — narrower than the tier band it wraps (the width restatement the W1 fold missed)
evidence: assist.odin:425-426: `width := (tier_pipe_width(v, bundles.bundle_tier[bi]) + f32(bundles.bundle_count[bi] - 1) * BUNDLE_EXTRA_WIDTH) * v.scale` / `halo := width + 6.0 * v.scale`; assist.odin:442-443: `width := tier_pipe_width(v, cand_tier) * v.scale` / `halo := width + 6.0 * v.scale` — vs the re-based siblings: view.odin:804 `halo := band_width(v, bundles.bundle_tier[bi], int(bundles.bundle_count[bi])) + 6 * v.scale // 7.1: the selection halo hugs the WIDE band` and view.odin:297 `band := band_width(v, tier, int(count))` (drawn width). assist.odin has no hunk in the diff.
detail: Band = wire×2.2; tier widths 3.5/5.5/8.5. A wide pipe's halo is 14.5px vs an 18.7px band — the glow sits inside the pipe, and the candidate halo pops on commit, contradicting its own comment.
recommended_fix: Derive both draw_glow_edge branches from band_width(): committed halo = band_width(...) + 6.0*v.scale; candidate halo = band_width(v, cand_tier, 1) + 6.0*v.scale.

title: palcheck re-implements harness internals it sits next to: normalize duplicates swizzle_rb + flip; the view init restates render_setup
evidence: palcheck.odin:78-82: `rl.ImageFlipVertical(img)` / `px := rl.LoadImageColors(img^)` / swap loop / `new_img.data = raw_data(px)` — identical body to goldens.odin:86-101 `swizzle_rb :: proc(img: ^rl.Image) {`; overlay.odin:117-118 shows the sharing pattern in the same package: `rl.ImageFlipVertical(&img)` / `swizzle_rb(&img)`. palcheck.odin:111-121: `palette := rnd.palette_load() ... view.font = rnd.load_hud_font(); if !rnd.sprites_load(&view.sprites) ... rnd.view_compute(&view, 1280, 720, &cat.balance)` restates goldens.odin:33-52 render_setup.
detail: Same package, both shareable — a sibling file already calls swizzle_rb directly. Two copies of subtle readback normalization plus a third sprite-fatal view init put drift risk inside the CI oracle itself.
recommended_fix: Delete normalize; call rl.ImageFlipVertical(&img) + swizzle_rb(&img) as overlay.odin does. Build a Render_Ctx and call render_setup (or extract a shared view-init proc) for the init block.

title: on_cancel fires before the placement branch — aborting an armed draw also snaps the camera home while the selection persists
evidence: exec.odin:47-58: `case Cancel:` / `if inp.on_cancel != nil { inp.on_cancel(inp.user, inp) } // 7.1: the camera-home exit (fires even when nothing is selected)` / ... / `if inp.placing >= 0 {` / `inp.placing = -1` / `inp.drag = {}` / `inp.drag.placing = -1` / `} else {` / `inp.sel_pipe = -1` / `inp.sel_node = -1` — the hook runs before the placing/deselect split, unconditionally.
detail: ESC/right-click during placement cancels the draw but keeps sel_node; the camera homes anyway and the selection-diff never refires — camera and selection state desync until the next interaction.
recommended_fix: Move the on_cancel call into the non-placing else branch. The W3 empty-selection case still fires there, and placement aborts stop moving the camera.

title: New chrome geometry now lives in two homes: the banner rect is render-owned, the SLA row rects are app-owned

detail: The 7.1 chrome idiom (render-package-owned layout, single-source rects) is followed for crisis_banner_rect but the SLA chip's rect and draw live in app/main.odin. Draw↔hit single-source holds in both; the split mirrors where each draw already lived.
recommended_fix: None now. When the fuller roster gets its proper panel (the code's own note), move the SLA rows into app/render alongside the popover and banner rects.
